metadata.title: सोनिया गांधी: आदिवासी का वजूद मिटाने पर तुली है सरकार | Sonia Gandhi raises alarm on Great Nicobar
metadata.description:
Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has raised strong objections to the ambitious Great Nicobar Project, warning that it poses a grave threat to the indigenous tribes of the island. Speaking on the issue, she expressed concern that the mega-development plan will uproot the Nicobarese and the Shompen, two vulnerable tribal communities whose lives and culture are deeply tied to the island’s forests and ecology.

Sonia Gandhi alleged that the central government has bypassed constitutional safeguards and legal provisions that exist to protect the rights of tribal communities. According to her, the project ignores crucial environmental and social concerns, and could lead to large-scale displacement, loss of traditional livelihoods, and the destruction of fragile ecosystems.

The Great Nicobar Project includes a transhipment port, an airport, township development, and power plants – initiatives that the government says will boost India’s strategic and economic position in the Indian Ocean. However, activists, tribal groups, and environmental experts have consistently flagged the risks of ecological imbalance and cultural extinction.

With Sonia Gandhi’s intervention, the debate around the project has once again intensified, raising urgent questions about development versus rights and survival of tribal communities in one of India’s most sensitive regions.
